items.title: Methane's GWP comparison
items.claim: Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 over short timescales. Approximately how does its 100-year global warming potential compare?

options.text: Around 28-30 times CO2 over 100 years (IPCC AR6)

items.reveal_title: About 28-30x over 100 years; closer to 80x over 20 years
items.reveal:
IPCC AR6 reports GWP-100 of around 27-30 for fossil and biogenic methane. Methane's atmospheric lifetime is about 12 years, making it a strong near-term lever.

The Global Methane Pledge (2021) targets a 30% cut by 2030.
items.why: Choice of GWP averaging window shapes how big methane appears to be as a problem.

items.title: Amazon dieback risk
items.claim: Research from the early 2020s suggests parts of the Amazon may be approaching a tipping point at what threshold of deforestation?
items.reveal:
Lovejoy and Nobre (2018) proposed a tipping point of 20-25% deforestation, combined with climate change, beyond which large parts of the Amazon could shift to savanna.

Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon stood near 17% by 2020 by INPE measurements.
items.why: Ecosystem tipping points have policy salience even when their exact value is uncertain.

items.title: Why the Montreal Protocol worked
items.claim: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out ozone-depleting substances. By the early 2020s what is the projected outcome?

options.text: The ozone layer is on track to recover to 1980 levels around mid-century outside the polar regions
The hole has expanded since the protocol

items.reveal:
WMO/UNEP scientific assessments (2018 and 2022) report stratospheric chlorine peaking in the late 1990s and recovery to 1980 ozone levels by around 2040 outside polar regions; 2066 over Antarctica.

Unreported CFC-11 emissions detected in 2018 were largely addressed by 2021.
items.why: A small group of carefully targeted treaties has produced large measurable atmospheric outcomes.
